hints.text: The dot product is a single number, not another vector. Matching components are multiplied, then those products are added.
Write the three products of matching components. One of them is zero. Add all three, and keep the sign of the last product.
The cross product is a vector perpendicular to both inputs. Each component is a $2\times 2$ determinant from the other rows.
The first component uses the lower-right square. The middle component is subtracted, not added. The last component uses the first two columns.

problems.prompt: Find the equation of the plane through $(1,0,-2)$ with normal vector $\langle 2,-1,3\rangle$.

hints.text: A normal and a point determine the plane. Every vector that lies in the plane is perpendicular to the normal, so their dot product is zero.
Write $\langle 2,-1,3\rangle\cdot\langle x-1,\, y-0,\, z-(-2)\rangle=0$, then expand and collect like terms. A constant multiple of the same equation is still the plane.

problems.prompt: Find the distance from the point $(1,2,2)$ to the plane $x+2y-2z+3=0$.

hints.text: Distance to a plane is the length of the projection onto the normal. Take an absolute value so the distance is not negative.
Evaluate $x+2y-2z+3$ at $(1,2,2)$, take the absolute value, and divide by the magnitude of $\langle 1,2,-2\rangle$.

problems.prompt: A line passes through $(1,-1,2)$ with direction $\langle 2,1,-1\rangle$. Give the point on the line at $t=1$.

hints.text: A line is a starting point plus a scalar times a direction. You only need the point that belongs to this one value of the parameter.
Add one copy of the direction $\langle 2,1,-1\rangle$ to the point $(1,-1,2)$. Keep the three components in order.
